title: Praia D'El Rey Settles All Three Prizes
title_candidates: Praia D'El Rey Settles All Three Prizes
Level, Then Lost: The Final Round
theme: A final round in which two of three prizes had been quietly decided for days, and the third briefly went level before swinging back inside four holes.
tone: wry, understated, faithful to the numbers
opening_hook: By the turn at Praia D'El Rey the TEG 9 Trophy had gone level for the first time all week — and by the 17th it very much hadn't.

round_story.subject: John Patterson's closing 47 stableford points, the best round of the final day
round_story.why_it_matters: Three days after a poor round had let his lead shrink, Patterson answered with the tournament's best round of golf to close out the TEG 9 Trophy.
round_story.shape: Patterson had stumbled to 34 points in round three, bottom half of the field and his lead down to three; he responded with a composed 47 in the final round, surviving a quintuple-bogey nine at the 5th to keep scoring throughout; the round stands as the day's best and the second-best of his brief four-round TEG career.
headline_candidates: Best Round Of A Nervy Day
round_story.standfirst: Three days after a wobble dropped him into the bottom half of the field, John Patterson produced the best round of the week when it mattered most.

race_story.subject: Alex Baker's brief level lead for the TEG 9 Trophy, undone by a back-nine collapse
race_story.why_it_matters: This was the only genuinely live race of the final round: Alex Baker produced personal bests in both formats and drew level for the Trophy, only for four ruinous holes to hand it straight back to John Patterson.
race_story.shape: Alex Baker arrived three points behind Patterson and playing the steadiest golf of the week; a string of pars drew him level for the Trophy lead at the 14th, but quadruple bogeys followed almost immediately at the 15th and 6th as part of an 11-shot bleed across holes 14-17; Patterson's own 47 closed the door, and Baker finishes runner-up by six despite a personal-best round.
headline_candidates: Level At The Turn, Undone Late
race_story.standfirst: A career-best card from Alex Baker briefly squared the TEG 9 Trophy race before four calamitous holes handed it straight back to John Patterson.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin's wire-to-wire TEG 9 Green Jacket, sealed with the best gross round of the day
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Mullin won every round of the week outright, extended his lead from seven to ten shots, and closed it out with the best gross score of the final round.
discovered_storylines.shape: Mullin arrived with a healthy Jacket lead already built on three round wins; an early quadruple bogey at the 1st threatened to open a door, but tidy pars through holes 2-4 and 7-9 restored order; he closes with a 16-over final round, the best gross score of the day, to complete a sweep in which he never finished worse than first.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: David Mullin's final-round 16-over capped a Green Jacket campaign in which he was never beaten in a single round all week.

discovered_storylines.subject: Stuart Neumann's rollercoaster final round confirms the TEG 9 Wooden Spoon
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A five-hole purple patch in the middle of the round briefly threatened an escape from the bottom of the table, but the closing holes made sure of the Spoon by a comfortable 16 shots.
discovered_storylines.shape: Neumann began the day already anchoring the table, 15 adrift of safety; he produced his best stretch of the week, 16 stableford points across holes 11-15, without dropping a gross shot; a quadruple bogey at the 16th and a further eight-shot bleed over the closing holes undid the recovery, and he finishes last by 16, almost exactly as he started the day.
headline_candidates: A Flash Of Form, Then Ruin
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A blistering five-hole stretch in the middle of the round threatened an escape from the bottom of the TEG 9 standings, but the closing holes made sure of the Wooden Spoon regardless.

race_state_note: The Green Jacket and Wooden Spoon placings had been effectively settled for days; only the Trophy's destination was genuinely live going into the last round.
